A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 20 readable pages including Appendices A–F. Full-text comparison and page rendering establish identical content on pages 2–20; page 1 differs only in an affiliation marker and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original corpus analysis and evaluations of Simba models for ASR, TTS and spoken language identification, including Tables 2–3 and F.1–F.2.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original corpus analysis and Simba model evaluation results in the main text and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 5.2 retains identical Simba-ASR multilingual fine-tuning, language-specific MMS-TTS adaptation and AfriHuBERT-based Simba-SLID procedures. No method components change.

E1.justification: The same datasets, languages, domains and ASR, TTS and SLID tasks are retained. Table 1, Appendices A–B and the evaluation tables contain identical coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2/F.1 retain the same MMS, Seamless, Whisper and WhisperT comparator columns. The MMS-TTS and MMS-LID-1024 evaluations in Tables 3 and F.2 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The splits, per-language sampling, preprocessing, checkpoint selection and training settings remain identical in Sections 3–5 and Appendices C–E. WER/CER and SLID macro-F1 reporting are unchanged.

E4.justification: The resource-distribution analysis and comparisons across datasets and language families are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes ablations, sensitivity tests or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions use identical point-estimate reporting for model evaluations, without reported repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported findings are identical, including the full appendix tables. For example, Simba-S remains at 41.65/18.3 overall WER/CER in Table F.1, and Simba-SLID remains at 70.82 overall macro-F1 in Table F.2.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs. The descriptive methodology and metric descriptions remain identical, with no mathematical definitions, assumptions or derivations added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: SimbaBench, resource-coverage analysis, baseline evaluation and the Simba model family. Their performance and inclusion claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7 retains the same interpretations concerning data quality, domain differences, model coverage and linguistic relatedness. Section 9 retains all limitations concerning representation bias, task coverage, modeling scope and implementation constraints.

D1.justification: Preprocessing instructions, model identifiers, hyperparameters and software references in Appendices C–E are identical. Section 4 also retains the same dataset-release statements, with no changed code or data access information.

R1.justification: The literature review, citations and bibliography are identical. Positioning relative to African speech resources and existing multilingual models does not change.

P1.justification: On page 1, v3 removes the MBZUAI affiliation marker from Muhammad Abdul-Mageed and updates the arXiv stamp from v1, 24 May 2025 to v3, 4 July 2025. Scientific prose, terminology and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4 and all main-text and appendix tables retain identical displays, captions and placement. The affiliation and version-stamp edits do not alter the document's layout structure.

improvement.justification: The methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, reproducibility information and appendices are unchanged. The affiliation-marker removal and updated arXiv stamp establish no meaningful improvement or deterioration in the paper's scientific quality or readability.
